{{small|(Nationwide)}} | terr_chan_10 = Channel 6 | website = {{URL|gmanetwork.com/gtv}} }} '''GTV''' (standing for '''Good TeleVision''', stylized as '''Gtv''') is a Philippine [[Terrestrial television|free-to-air]] [[Television broadcaster|television network]] owned and operated by [[Citynet Network Marketing and Productions|Citynet Network Marketing and Productions Inc.]], a wholly owned subsidiary of [[GMA Network (company)|GMA Network, Inc.]] It was launched on February 22, 2021, replacing [[GMA News TV]] on its flagship station, [[DWDB-TV|DWDB-TV UHF Channel 27]], and its relay stations across the [[Philippines]]. It is the sixth overall secondary television brand of GMA Network since 1995, as Citynet Television. The network produces programs from studios located at the [[GMA Network Center]], [[EDSA]] corner Timog Avenue, Diliman, [[Quezon City]]. The network's primary transmitter facility is located at the [[Tower of Power (transmitter)|GMA Tower of Power]] site, Barangay Culiat, Tandang Sora, Quezon City. ==History== ===As GMA News TV (2011–2021)=== GTV was previously known as [[GMA News TV]], a channel focused on all-news and public service, as part of [[GMA Integrated News|GMA News and Public Affairs]]' plans to expand its presence on free-to-air television as well as retaining some lifestyle and public affairs programs from its predecessor, [[Q (Philippine TV network)|QTV/Q]]. The channel was unveiled on February 7, 2011, on ''[[24 Oras]]'', GMA's flagship nightly newscast. The news channel launched on February 28, 2011.{{cite news |title=GMA-7 launches GMA News TV on Channel 11 |url=https://www.pep.ph/guide/tv/7578/gma-7-launches-gma-news-tv-on-channel-11 |access-date=November 1, 2020 |work=PEP.ph |date=February 2, 2011}}{{cite news |title=GMA Network launches GMA News TV |url=https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/money/content/212269/gma-network-launches-gma-news-tv/story/ |access-date=November 1, 2020 |work=GMA News Online |date=February 5, 2011}}{{cite news |title=GMA News TV goes on air |url=https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/news/nation/214089/gma-news-tv-goes-on-air/story/ |access-date=November 1, 2020 |work=GMA News Online |date=February 28, 2011}} It launched a wide variety of news and public affairs and entertainment-produced programs to serve its audience. From its launch to 2019, [[ZOE Broadcasting Network]] served as an originating affiliate and flagship station of GMA News TV, as a result of a blocktime lease agreement between ZOE Broadcasting and GMA's subsidiary Citynet Network Marketing and Productions in 2005, allowing the latter to lease the entire airtime of [[DZOE-TV|DZOE-TV 11 Manila]], in exchange for upgrading the former's facilities and an off-peak timeslot for its programs on Channel 11 and [[GMA Network]].{{cite news |url=https://www.philstar.com/business/2005/04/28/275585/gma-network-partners-zoe-broadcasting-channel-11 |title=GMA Network partners with Zoe Broadcasting Channel 11 |publisher=[[The Philippine Star]] |date=April 28, 2005 |access-date=April 28, 2005 |work=Philstar}} However, due to increasing lease payments of GMA Network to ZOE Broadcasting, which is accompanied by decreased revenues of GMA, the two networks announced on April 24, 2019, that they will terminate the agreement by the end of May 2019. As a result, GMA News TV Manila was reassigned to analog [[DWDB-TV|Channel 27]], which was being used for the digital test broadcast of GMA Network, on June 4. In turn, DTV operations of GMA were transferred to a permanent frequency, UHF Channel 15 (479.143 MHz), which had been MHz), which was being used since May 15.{{cite news |last=Melegrito |first=JM |title=ZOE Broadcasting to end Blocktime Agreement with GMA Network |url=https://www.dtvpilipinas.org/2019/04/28/zoe-broadcasting-to-end-blocktime-agreement-with-gma-network/ |access-date=November 1, 2020 |work=DTV Pilipinas |date=April 28, 2019 |archive-date=April 28, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190428033825/https://www.dtvpilipinas.org/2019/04/28/zoe-broadcasting-to-end-blocktime-agreement-with-gma-network/ |url-status=dead }} In line with the government's protocol of imposing the [[enhanced community quarantine in Luzon]] (also known as "Luzon Lockdown") due to the outbreak of [[COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines]], GMA News TV temporarily went off-air on March 19, 2020{{cite web |title=GMA News TV temporarily goes off the air amid Luzon lockdown |url=https://cnnphilippines.com/news/2020/3/18/GMA-News-TV-COVID-19.html |work=CNN Philippines |access-date=March 19, 2020 |date=March 18, 2020 |archive-date=June 12, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200612174933/https://cnnphilippines.com/news/2020/3/18/GMA-News-TV-COVID-19.html |url-status=dead }}{{cite news |last=Aguilar |first=Krissy |title=GMA News TV temporarily signs off due to 'current state of calamity' |url=https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1244761/gma-news-tv-temporarily-signs-off-due-to-current-state-of-calamity |work=Inquirer.net |access-date=March 19, 2020 |language=en |date=March 19, 2020}} and returned on-air two days later, March 21, with limited broadcasting hours, with ''Dobol B sa News TV'' as a provisional programming, expanding its broadcast (for the first time, wherein the afternoon programming of [[DZBB-AM|DZBB]] was introduced and included in the program lineup) from Mondays to Sundays from 6:00 am to afternoon until the simulcast of ''[[24 Oras]]'' (both weekday and weekend edition) and [[Sign-on and sign-off|signs-off]] right after the newscast.{{cite web |last=Mendoza |first=Red |title=GMA News TV, CNN Philippines to return on air |url=https://www.manilatimes.net/2020/03/20/news/latest-stories/gma-news-tv-cnn-philippines-to-return-on-air/704756/ |work=The Manila Times |access-date=March 24, 2020 |date=March 20, 2020}} On April 13, 2020, the channel resumed its regular primetime programming after ''[[24 Oras]]'', with the launch of ''New Normal: The Survival Guide'', and ''Power Block: Serbisyong Totoo on Primetime'' as its provisional primetime blocktime. GMA News TV's programming was fully restored by September 21, 2020. On November 21, 2020, Sports Interactive Network, an [[GMA New Media|affiliate news portal of GMA]], published an article that the network announced plans for a possible reformat of GMA News TV into a news, sports and variety channel, which is similar to the old format of Citynet Television and QTV. The plans were unveiled following GNTV's [[Channel drift|gradual shift]] away from its original news and public affairs channel format and towards "general" entertainment and sports since September 2020, which includes acquisition of broadcast rights to [[National Collegiate Athletic Association (Philippines)|NCAA]] and [[Philippine Super Liga|PSL]] games (the main reason of GTV's rebrand), a simulcast of its sister digital channel [[Hallypop (Philippine TV channel)|Hallypop]] (until it cancelled in the fourth quarter of 2020), and additional entertainment programs from its mother station [[GMA Network]] due to increase of its commercial loads.{{Cite web|title=GMA 7 beats TV5 for right to broadcast NCAA games, says source|url=https://www.spin.ph/life/guide/gma-7-beats-tv5-for-rights-to-broadcast-ncaa-games-says-source-a791-20201119|access-date=November 21, 2020|website=Spin.ph|language=en}} These changes were embattled by mounting viewer criticisms, notably when the country was hit by [[Typhoon Goni|Typhoon Goni (Rolly)]], where Asian dramas, cartoons and anime were aired instead of pre-empting them for [[24-hour news cycle|round-the-clock news coverage]].{{Cite web |last=Anarcon |first=James Patrick |date=November 1, 2020 |title=GMA News TV trends on Twitter as netizens look for updates about 22, 2021|website=[[YouTube]]}} According to some of the GMA executives in their media conference, which took place in the days before GTV launched, they took one year to plan on relaunching the channel as GTV due to the needs of its viewers and more variety for "young-at-heart" viewers. While retaining most in-house programs of its predecessor, GTV carries news and public affairs with the addition of entertainment, variety, lifestyle and sports programs, which is similar to the old format of what Citynet Television and [[Q (Philippine TV network)|QTV/Q]] had done before. [[GMA News TV|The international counterpart of GTV's predecessor]] is still operational even after February 28, 2021, a decade after its original domestic counterpart was launched. Unlike its predecessor, the channel uses [[Taglish]]. On February 27, 2023, GTV, along with other GMA Network-owned channels, switched its broadcast from the original 4:3 format to 16:9 [[anamorphic widescreen]] format. This change allowed for a widescreen presentation, optimizing the viewing experience for viewers with compatible widescreen televisions.{{cite web|title=Kapuso shows now available for widescreen viewing beginning February 27|url=https://www.gmanetwork.com/entertainment/showbiznews/news/98539/kapuso-shows-now-available-for-widescreen-viewing-beginning-february-27/story|website=GMA Network|date=February 24, 2023|access-date=February 25, 2023}} ====Partnership with ABS-CBN (2023–2024)==== On June 20, 2023, [[GMA Network (company)|GMA Network, Inc.]] collaborated with [[ABS-CBN Corporation]] for the simulcast of the noontime variety program ''[[It's Showtime (Philippine TV program)|It's Showtime]]'' on GTV.{{Cite web | date= June 20, 2023 | title=Bulaga! GTV (standing for Good TeleVision, stylized as Gtv) is a Philippine free-to-air television network owned and operated by Citynet Network Marketing and Productions Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary of GMA Network, Inc. It was launched on February 22, 2021, replacing GMA News TV on its flagship station, DWDB-TV UHF Channel 27, and its relay stations across the Philippines.
It is the sixth overall secondary television brand of GMA Network since 1995, as Citynet Television. The network produces programs from studios located at the GMA Network Center, EDSA corner Timog Avenue, Diliman, Quezon City. The network's primary transmitter facility is located at the GMA Tower of Power site, Barangay Culiat, Tandang Sora, Quezon City.
